title: Ledger sequence stamp on every JSON response plus work show --since
description: Context: a 2h47m dabble-employee-app agent session made 300 CLI calls with 24 failures. Failure clusters: 117 read-only work show polls (~40% of all calls), 14 identical failed sync refresh retries, 6 vault init retries, 66 agent finish calls with only 2 standalone evidence records, 6 NOT_FOUND finish/release (ownership confusion), 1 CONFLICT claim, 2 POLICY_VIOLATION sprint closes. Design principle for this mission: every response (success or error) must carry enough state that the correct next action is derivable without another read, and the honest path (evidence, ownership, health) must be the path of least resistance. Problem: agents cannot cheaply establish that nothing changed, so they re-read full state. Change: stamp every --json response envelope with the current ledger sequence (the append-ordered position already maintained by the ledgers in .boreal/ledgers). Add work show <id> --since <seq> which returns a minimal {unchanged:true, seq} payload when no event newer than seq touches that work item. Where: response envelope composer in packages/engine/src/runtime.ts, work show handler in apps/cli/src/commands.ts, command-registry.ts usage strings, docs/cli/COMMANDS.md. Constraint: the seq must come from the durable ledger ordering, not the sqlite cache, so it is stable across cache rebuilds.
acceptanceCriteria: Every --json response envelope includes a ledger sequence field
work show --since <seq> returns a minimal unchanged payload when nothing newer touches the item, and full state otherwise
Sequence survives a cache rebuild (test proves seq is ledger-derived, not cache-derived)
